subject.title: Feature Request: Plugin Circuit Breaker for graceful degradation

question: Should OpenClaw add a core framework-level plugin circuit breaker, and what default fail modes, storage model, status output, and operator reset controls are acceptable for existing plugins?
rationale: The code gap is real, but choosing active quarantine semantics affects plugin API contracts, persisted state, config/defaults, operator commands, and compatibility for existing plugin behavior.

options.title: Design Core Breaker First
options.body: Keep this issue open for a maintainer-led design covering hook/tool attribution, SQLite-backed state, status/reset commands, passive telemetry, and compatibility-safe default behavior before implementation.

options.title: Keep Breakers Plugin-Owned
options.body: Defer a framework breaker and ask high-risk plugins to implement degradation through current hook/config surfaces, accepting duplicated reliability policy per plugin.

options.title: Start Passive Telemetry Only
options.body: Add shared timing/failure attribution and log-only breaker evaluation first, then decide active open/half-open quarantine behavior after deployment data.

recommendation.title: Design Core Breaker First
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open for a maintainer-led design covering hook/tool attribution, SQLite-backed state, status/reset commands, passive telemetry, and compatibility-safe default behavior before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The central current-main hook runner, global runner, status, and runtime surfaces route most directly to vincentkoc's recent merged work.
